records.text: Pattern: fork. Attacker count: one. Target count: several. Follow the shared attacker.
Issue: a fork setup becomes available to the other side. Attacker count: one. Exposed targets: multiple.
Missed resource: a fork. Another move offered a way to attack several targets with one piece.
Mechanism detected: king pin. Leaving the line would expose the king, so that movement is not legal.
Alert: the other side gains access to a king pin. Constraint: a pinned piece is held on that line by its king.
Missed pattern: a pin to the king, available with an alternative. Constraint it would have set: pinned piece locked to its line.
Pattern: skewer. Front unit displaced; rear unit left open on that line.
Alert: skewer geometry now available to the other side. Front unit moves; rear unit becomes reachable.
Missed pattern: skewer. A stronger move contained it. Front unit forced aside; rear unit exposed.
Objective: capture the defender. Identify what it protects, then compare the position without it.
Alert: one defender has become a capture target for the other side. What it guards could then lose that protection.
Missed resource: capturing a defender. Another move offered a way to remove protection from what it guards.
The pattern is back-rank mate. Escape squares: occupied by the king's own pieces. Follow how the attack reaches it.
Alert: back-rank mate route open for the other side. Escape barrier: the king's own pieces.
A route to back-rank mate was available. This move passes up that finishing pattern.
The objective is promotion. Track the pawn's path to the last rank. Output there: a new piece.
Issue: a promotion route is now open for the other side. Follow the pawn that could reach the last rank.
Missed resource: promotion. A stronger move offered a route for a pawn to reach the last rank.
One piece moves aside, uncovering an attack from another. That is the discovered-attack pattern.
Alert: discovered-attack geometry unlocked for the other side. One piece steps aside; a hidden attacker activates.
Missed pattern: a discovered attack, available with another move. Moving the blocker would uncover a threat from a different piece.
Mechanism: double attack, two threats active together. Track how the two threat vectors interact.
Issue: the other side gains a double-attack option. Both attacks need attention.
Missed pattern: a double attack, available with a stronger move. Combined threat count in this move: below that.
Pattern: deflection. Step one: draw a defender off its task. Step two: use the gap.
Alert: defender diversion possible for the other side. Its original task could then go unattended.
Missed pattern: deflection, available with another move. Defender task left undisturbed.
Objective: take a piece with zero guards. Locate the loose target before evaluating the capture.
An undefended capture was available in another line. This move misses the opportunity to take that loose piece.
Issue: an undefended piece is now capturable by the other side. Check which piece could be left without protection.
Cause: the only effective defender moves away. Result: the other side can capture the piece it was guarding.
The previous move supplied the warning. This move leaves that attack unanswered, so the threatened piece can be captured.
The first capture is only part of the exchange. The recapture takes a more valuable piece. Count both sides.
A minor piece leaves its starting square and enters play. Development recorded.
Alternative output: development of one minor piece off its home square.
The rook now occupies an open file. Pawn count on that file: zero, for both colors.
The alternative would leave a rook on an open file, containing no pawns of either color.
The rook occupies a semi-open file. Friendly pawns are absent from it; enemy pawns remain.
Alternative output: a rook on a file holding enemy pawns and none of its own. Enemy pawns would remain there, but no friendly pawns.
Passed pawn registered. Enemy pawns able to block or capture it: zero.
Alternative output: a passed pawn. Enemy pawns able to block or capture it: zero.
Passed pawn, prior status confirmed. This move pushes it one square nearer the last rank. Compare its new position with the old one.
Alternative output: one more step for the pawn that was already passed. Compare its destination on the board.
An isolated pawn remains in the position. Neither neighboring file contains a friendly pawn.
Alternative output: an isolated pawn. Adjacent-file friendly pawns: zero.
Support added. A piece that lacked a defender now has one.
The alternative would add support to a piece that was undefended before the move.
A piece is now undefended. That describes its support, not proof that it can be won.
Alternative output: one undefended piece. That alone would not prove a winning capture.
King flight squares: plus one. Compare the positions to see which change made it available.
The alternative would give the king a new legal flight square. Compare what would change around it.
Castling executed. King and rook both change position.
Unused option: castling. It would relocate the king and rook together.
Bishop pair status: broken by this capture. Square colors covered by that side's bishops: one.
Alternative output: one bishop captured, opposing pair dissolved.
Doubled pawns remain in the position. Pawns of the same color occupy the same file.
Alternative output: a file holding two pawns of a single color.
Alert: forced checkmate sequence detected for the other side. Trace the attack to find where the defense fails.
A forced checkmate was available. This move loses that finish. Return to the position and locate it.
Sacrifice checked. Acceptance test in the examined line: passed.
Playable moves found: one, this one. Every other examined choice: losing.
Advantage-preserving moves found: one, this one. Every other examined choice: losing.
A capture is available on the immediate reply. Check what the other side can take.
Top reply detected: check. Responding to the threat to the king takes priority.
Engine preference: a different move. Compare its replies on the board.
This move scores below the best option in the engine comparison. Inspect the reply for the difference.
Rating: strong, within the set of moves the engine examined.
Sound choice. It retains much of the position's value, though the engine prefers another move.
Human-model label: unusual. Engine label: strong. No contradiction.
The human-move model and examined alternatives indicate a difficult move to find. Keep the pattern for future reference.
Defense found. The position remains playable. Human-model and search difficulty score for this defense: high.
Human-move estimate: natural. Engine comparison: best move. Both tests agree here.
Human-model tag: natural. Engine tag: strong; preferred move differs.
Clock reading before this move: low.
Clock log: fast decision, time remaining.
The clock records substantial time spent on this decision.
Opening sequence matched. Line status: recognized.
Opening-book boundary reached. This is the first move beyond the recognized line.
Recovery confirmed. Setback offset. Playability back online.
A playable position is restored. Contributing factor: errors by the other side.
The opponent supplied an opportunity on the previous move. This move uses it.
The previous move supplied an opportunity. This response leaves it unused. Compare the stronger reply.
This issue has appeared earlier in the reviewed game. Compare the examples for a recurring warning sign.
Protection restored. Defender assigned to the previously unguarded piece.
The damage is cumulative. Concession count: several small ones, this move included.
Conversion log: advantage maintained across the reviewed moves, ending in the recorded win. Follow that stretch to examine the conversion.
Pattern match: same issue logged in other saved games. Compare those examples with this one.
Checkmate confirmed. Legal king moves remaining: zero. Attack complete.
Checkmate confirmed. King escape squares available: none. Review the earlier defense for an intervention point.
Draw confirmed. The result is settled; earlier decisions remain available for review.
Position ready. Examine the board and select a move.
That attempt is not accepted. Recheck the position and try another move.
No analysis result was received. Return to the move to retry the request.
The saved engine analysis finds forced checkmate for the side that made this move.
Saved engine analysis, post-move: forced-mate flag raised for the other side.
Across the saved line, the moving side gains material relative to the starting position.
Across the saved line, the moving side loses material relative to the starting position.
Exercise status: accepted. The displayed moves do not establish a clear tactical explanation.
Exercise status: not accepted. A clear tactical reason is not established by the displayed moves.
Saved answer matched. Acceptance here is defined by the exercise's saved answers.
No saved answer matched. That does not prove a different legal move is bad chess.
Examine the move before proceeding to the next position.
Correct. Retain the reason as well as the move.
Practice recorded. Schedule change: none.
Solved. Relearning status remains in place for this recall.
Starting position. The moves under examination begin here.
Next move displayed. Examine the changed position.
Check. The threat to the king requires an answer.
The king is no longer in check after this move.
Promotion completed. Pawn converted to a new piece at the last rank.
Promotion completed, with check. Required next action: answer the check.
Promotion and checkmate. King moves available: zero.
Promotion executed. The resulting position also removes the check against its king.
A piece is captured by this move.
Capture completed, with check. Both changes belong to this move.
The capture delivers checkmate. No legal escape remains for the king.
This capture ends the check against the moving side's king.
Pawn capture executed at the last rank, followed by promotion. Both actions completed.
Pawn capture, then promotion on the last rank. Check is included in the same move.
Capture, promotion, checkmate. The king has no legal escape from the resulting position.
The pawn captures and promotes. That move also ends the check against its king.
Castling executed: king shifted two squares, rook transferred beside it. Check status: delivered by the same move.
Castling executed: king shifted two squares, rook transferred beside it. Checkmate: opposing king moves available, zero.
Fork sequence: single attacker, multiple targets, one captured. Net material balance in the example: positive.
The indicated capture is illegal because of the pin to the king. Line exit would leave the king in check.
Attacked unit status: king-pinned. Its escape is restricted to moves that do not expose the king.
The defenders cannot recapture there: doing so would expose their king. Line result: material gain.
Pinned piece status: locked to the line by its king. Follow the moves to see it captured.
The front piece moves off the line. The piece behind it is then captured along that same line.
The king leaves the line to escape check. Example result: the same attacker collects the unit behind it.
The only defender is captured. Later in the shown moves, the piece it guarded is captured as well.
The defender leaves its task. Guarded unit: captured next. Deflection demonstrated.
The blocker moves, and the piece behind it gains an open attack line. Capture executed along that line.
The moving piece clears the line. Another piece now gives check through the opening.
Double check. Both pieces attack the king at the same time.
Attack vector one: the moved piece. Attack vector two: the line it opened. Example outcome: target collected by the second attacker.
Follow the promotion. Example balance for the promoting side: material up.
The undefended piece is captured in this example. A net material gain for the capturing side is also established.
The opponent's preceding move released the attacker from a relative pin. The target stayed in place and is captured in the shown line.
The marked reply is legal for the other side. Play it to examine the next position.
Pre-move scan: list friendly pieces that can be captured without a useful recapture.
Inspect loose enemy pieces before selecting a quiet move.
Scan forcing moves for one piece with two valuable targets in range. Track the shared attacker.
Pre-move scan for a pinned piece: identify what lies behind it. Possible values: king, or higher-value piece.
Look behind the first target. An attack may expose a valuable piece farther along the line.
Before exchanging a defender, identify what depends on its protection.
Pre-move scan: for each blocking piece that moves, register the opened lines.
Search for a move that combines two threats. Include checks and newly opened lines.
Before moving a back-rank defender, inspect the king's escape squares.
Count the moves required for promotion. Check the forcing pawn advances.
Before moving a defender, identify every piece that will lose its protection.
Compare the value captured with the value lost to the recapture. Evaluate the whole exchange.
Test each forcing exchange: does it pull a defender off a second target?
The saved answers set the exercise's acceptance rule. Moves outside that list are not flagged as bad chess by default.
These moves demonstrate play against strong replies. Strong is not a synonym for forced.
Material scope: the shown line only, from the line's own start. The written notes specify the piece values.
Saved line scan: no simple tactical reason established. Compare the replies directly; positional cause: none inferred.
The saved answer policy governs this explanation. Setting location: the written notes.
The moves from the opening line under study are now displayed.
Match confirmed with the selected study material.
Select a move from the chosen study lines.
Any move from the selected opening lines is accepted here.
Input requested: the move your study material lists next.
Lookup failed: move absent from the selected opening lines. Choose another move.
Lookup result: no match in the selected lines. Retry is available. Schedule impact for the edited study: none from this saved attempt.
Lookup result: no match in the selected lines. Retry is available. Retired position: its review dates stay fixed.
Mixed Due accepts moves from this line. Dedicated practice restricts answers to this line alone.
Scheduled recalls request moves for the selected side. Active studies share a single card when they share a position.
Saved session reload required before the next move.
Playback running: the verified line, move by move.
Attempt recorded as revealed. The solution can be replayed below.
Solution completed after a retry. The record retains the earlier miss and the successful finish.
Full solution correct. No wrong moves recorded. Pattern resolved.
Move rejected: not the puzzle solution. Prior correct moves: stored.
Move accepted. Find the next move required by the puzzle.
Position ready. Calculate before submitting a move.
Engine data is insufficient for an explanation here.
Review paused. Resume below, or move a piece to probe the position.
Select a move to inspect it, or move a piece to run a test line.
